title: Correctness of the TMSAT reduction
statement: Let $c$ be a machine representation scheme, let $L,V$ be languages of bit strings, let $C,e$ be natural numbers, let $\alpha$ be a bit string, and let $T : \mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that for every bit string $x$, membership $x\in L$ is equivalent to the existence of a bit string $u$ with $|u|=C(|x|+1)^e$ and $x u\in V$. Suppose also that for every such $x,u$, the machine decoded from $\alpha$ halts within $T(|x|)$ steps on input $\langle x,u\rangle$ and outputs the single bit indicating whether $x u\in V$. Then for every bit string $x$, $x\in L$ if and only if $\langle\alpha,\langle x,\langle1^{C(|x|+1)^e},1^{T(|x|)}\rangle\rangle\rangle$ belongs to $\mathrm{TMSAT}_c$.
hypotheses_covered: For every $x$, $x\in L$ iff some $u$ of length $C(|x|+1)^e$ has $xu\in V$
For every $x,u$ of that length, the machine decoded from $\alpha$ computes the indicator of $xu\in V$ on input $\langle x,u\rangle$ within $T(|x|)$ steps
replaced: Let $c$ be a machine-representation scheme, which assigns to every bit string $\alpha$ a one-work-tape binary Turing machine $M_\alpha$ (decoding is total). Let $L$ and $V$ be languages of bit strings, $C, e \in \mathbb{N}$, $\alpha$ a bit string and $T \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$. Suppose that $x \in L$ if and only if some $u$ with $|u| = C(|x|+1)^e$ satisfies $xu \in V$, and that for all $x, u$ with $|u| = C(|x|+1)^e$, $M_\alpha$ on input $\langle x,u\rangle$ halts within $T(|x|)$ steps with output the single bit $[xu \in V]$. Then for every bit string $x$, $x \in L$ if and only if $\langle\alpha,\langle x,\langle 1^{C(|x|+1)^e},1^{T(|x|)}\rangle\rangle\rangle \in \mathrm{TMSAT}_c$, where $\langle a,b\rangle$ is the self-delimiting pair encoding, $1^k$ the word of $k$ ones, and $\mathrm{TMSAT}_c$ the set of strings $\langle\beta,\langle y,\langle 1^n,1^t\rangle\rangle\rangle$ such that $M_\beta$ halts on $\langle y,v\rangle$ within $t$ steps with output exactly $1$ for some $v$ with $|v| = n$.
